children: You are about to pay a Rs 20,000 bill at a shop when the cashier tells you that using your credit card will cost an extra 2 percent. Pay through UPI or cash, however, and there is no additional charge.
It is something many card users come across, especially when making larger purchases. But what exactly is this extra amount, and are you supposed to pay it?

The answer is not quite as straightforward as it may seem. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has said that it has not issued specific instructions on the levy of charges on credit card transactions. Card payments are also governed by agreements between merchants, banks, payment companies and card networks.
Why does the shop want extra money?
When you pay by credit card, the merchant usually has to pay a fee for accepting that payment. This is commonly referred to as the Merchant Discount Rate, or MDR.

The merchant does not simply hand the entire amount to your bank. The cost of processing a card transaction is shared across different parts of the payment system, including the card-issuing bank, the acquiring bank or payment provider and the card network.
Some businesses try to recover this cost by adding a percentage to the customer's bill.
So when a shop asks for an additional 2 percent for paying by card, it is generally trying to pass some or all of its card-acceptance cost on to you.
Does RBI ban credit card surcharges?
This is where consumers need to be careful about sweeping claims.
RBI has specifically stated, in responses to queries on the issue, that it has not issued instructions on the levy of charges on credit card transactions.
That is different from saying every credit card surcharge is automatically permitted.

The merchant's agreement with its bank, payment provider or card network may contain its own rules about whether such a charge can be passed on to customers. So if a shop asks you to pay extra, you can question the charge and, if necessary, raise the issue with your card issuer.
Debit cards are different
Do not assume the same rules apply to debit and credit cards.

RBI has issued specific directions covering MDR on debit card transactions. Its framework has required banks and payment participants to ensure that merchants do not pass debit-card MDR on to customers.
So the fact that both cards are being used on the same machine does not mean the regulatory position is identical.
What about a 'convenience fee'?
You may also encounter a convenience or service fee, particularly when booking tickets or paying for services online.

This is not necessarily the same thing as a shop simply adding a "credit card charge". RBI's card directions say that a convenience fee charged on specific transactions should be shown transparently before the transaction. Its payment aggregator rules also require charges other than the price of the product or service to be clearly displayed before payment.
That is why it is worth checking the final amount before entering your PIN or approving an online payment.
Why do some shops prefer UPI?
Cost is one reason businesses may encourage you to scan a UPI QR code instead.

For consumers, UPI payments remain free. The government said in August 2026 that even if MDR is introduced for some merchant transactions in future, consumers will not be charged and most merchant transactions will continue to remain free.
This can make UPI cheaper for a merchant to accept than a credit card.
What should you do if a shop adds a card charge?
Ask what the additional amount is for before paying. Check the final bill and payment amount rather than noticing the surcharge after the transaction is complete.

If you believe you have been wrongly charged, you can first take it up with the merchant and your card issuer. RBI says that if a cardholder is unhappy with the issuer's response, or does not receive a response within a month, they can approach the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme.
The simplest rule at the billing counter is this: don't automatically accept an unexplained "card charge". Ask what you are paying for before you tap, swipe or enter your PIN.

title: Shop asking you to pay extra for using a credit card? Here’s what you should know
